name: Leaning Dumbbell Lateral Raise
description: The leaning lateral raise is performed by holding a fixed support with one hand and leaning the body away, then raising a dumbbell with the free arm in a lateral arc. The lateral lean places the medial deltoid under a greater stretch at the bottom position and creates a more consistent resistance profile throughout the range of motion compared to a vertical stance. This enhanced stretch at the bottom makes it one of the most effective dumbbell lateral raise variations for medial deltoid hypertrophy.

execution.starting_position: Stand beside an upright support (rack post, cable column). Grip the support with the inside hand. Lean the body away from the support, creating a straight angled line from feet to head. Hold a dumbbell in the outside hand with arm hanging down.
execution.setup_instructions: The lean angle determines the bottom stretch — a greater lean creates a greater stretch. Begin with a moderate lean of 15-20 degrees.
steps: Step 1: Hold the support, lean away, dumbbell at the side.
Step 2: Raise the dumbbell laterally in an arc from the hanging position.
Step 3: Raise until the arm is parallel to the floor.
Step 4: Lower slowly under control, letting the dumbbell hang for a full stretch.
Step 5: Complete all reps, switch sides.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the raise, inhale on the lowering.
common_mistakes: Not using the full hang at the bottom — the stretch is a key advantage of this variation
Excessive trap shrug at the top
safety_considerations: Ensure the fixed support is stable before leaning
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full hang at the bottom (enhanced stretch position), raise to shoulder height.
coaching_cues: Let it hang fully at the bottom
Raise from the elbow, not the wrist
Feel the stretch — that's the point
